The graph above shows the velocity of an object moving in a straight line along the $x$-axis. At time $t=1$ the particle is located at the position $x=2.$ What is the position of the particle at time $t=5?$
question.worked_solution:
The position of the particle at $t=5$ is equal to its position at $t=1$ plus the total displacement over $t\in [1,5].$ Therefore, we can calculate it as follows:

$$
x(5)=x(1)+{\int }_{1}^{5}v(t)\,\text{d}t
$$

We are told that $x(1)=2,$ and we can compute the integral ${\int }_{1}^{5}v(t)\,\text{d}t$ by finding the signed area under the graph from $t=1$ to $t=5.$ Computing the signed area, we get

$$
{\int }_{1}^{5}v(t)\,\text{d}t=6.
$$

Therefore,

$$
x(5)=2+6=8.
$$

So, the position of the particle at $t=5$ is $x=8.$
